test_title: PYST 10: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A car travels a distance of 120 km at a speed of 20 km/hr and returns the same distance at a speed of 30 km/hr. What is the average speed of the car for the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **distance** covered is the same for two different speeds, the average speed is the **harmonic mean** of the speeds.

Average Speed = (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 20 × 30) ÷ (20 + 30)

Average Speed = 1200 ÷ 50 = 24 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance for one way = 120 km

Speed during onward journey (v₁) = 20 km/hr

Speed during return journey (v₂) = 30 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fbf34acf421037549a984a345c90d884c83e84becb8a3da3ef444f08deda886f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken for onward journey (t₁) = 120 ÷ 20 = 6 hours

⇒ Time taken for return journey (t₂) = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 hours

⇒ Total distance covered = 120 + 120 = 240 km

⇒ Total time taken = 6 + 4 = 10 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 240 ÷ 10 = 24 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General Case)

For unequal distances d₁, d₂ and times t₁, t₂, the average speed is (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂).

Equal Time Intervals

If a body travels at speed v₁ for time T and speed v₂ for the same time T, the average speed is the arithmetic mean: (v₁ + v₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

Relative speed is the speed of one object with respect to another. Same direction: v₁ − v₂ | Opposite direction: v₁ + v₂.</p
